docs.title: Advanced Tunnelling Laboratories
docs.text:
Welcome to the Advanced Tunnelling Laboratories repository. In this website, we aim to bring several laboratories focused on showcasing Tunnelling protocols.

This website contains two setup guides for the emulators used, GNS3 and ContainerLab, to help prepare the test environment.

There are also several guides, each focusing on a different Tunnelling protocol, providing a brief overview of the protocol and its features, explaining the emulator used, devices and topology chosen for the demonstration, the configurations needed for everything to run properly and then several questions to help the learning process.

We hope you enjoy these laboratories, and that they help you learn about Internet and its safety!

docs.title: Containerlab Setup
docs.text:
Containerlab is a container-based network emulation framework designed for rapid deployment of virtual networking laboratories.

It enables engineers to quickly build realistic network topologies using several router images, the most important for us being Nokia´s SR SIM.

Containerlab uses Docker and Linux networking primitives to interconnect virtual nodes with high performance and minimal resource consumption.

docs.title: Main Capabilities
docs.text:
• Fast Topology Deployment: Labs can be deployed in seconds using YAML topology definitions.

  • Multi-Vendor Support: Containerlab supports numerous network operating systems and Linux distributions.

  • Native Linux Networking: Containerlab uses Linux bridges, namespaces, Docker networking.

  • Automation Friendly: Topology files are fully declarative and integrate easily with Git, Ansible and Python automation.

  • Packet Captures: Packet captures can be performed directly through the CLI or through WireShark containers through ContainerLab´s VSCode extension.

docs.title: Recommended Environment
docs.text:
Containerlab is native to Linux, as such, we recommend using it in a native Linux computer, or running it in an Ubuntu VM, using VMware or VirtualBox.

Warning

Beware that large ContainerLab deployments might consume significant resources. As such, ensure that your device has the necessary resources to run ContainerLab, especially if it is a Virtual Machine.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before installing Containerlab, install:

  • Docker
  • VSCode

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The ContainerLab team has prepared a command that should install all necessary components:

curl -sL https://containerlab.dev/setup | sudo -E bash -s "all"

docs.title: VSCode Extensions
docs.text:
ContainerLab has an extension that allows it to be fully run through a GUI in VSCode. This is very helpful to start working in ContainerLab and performing the laboratories as simply as possible. Besides the ContainerLab extension, we recommend others that help making its usage significantly better:

Extension Purpose Containerlab Topology support YAML YAML syntax Docker Docker integration

docs.title: Installing the ContainerLab VSCode Extension
docs.text:
Open VSCode.

Navigate to:

Extensions → Search "Containerlab"

Install:

Containerlab
by srl-labs

docs.title: Features of the VSCode Extension
docs.text: The extension provides tools to visualize your topology and undeployed labs, deploy, destroy and redeploy your lab, access your devices through Shell and SSH and capture traffic between your devices with an in-built docker container with a WireShark image.

docs.title: Using Containerlab with VSCode
docs.text:
Create the folder where you want your lab to be in.

Explorer → New Folder → clab-test

Create a topology file:

clab-test.clab.yml

A base topology for two Alpine devices connected to each other is as follows:

name: clab-test

topology:
  nodes:
    r1:
      kind: linux
      image: alpine

    r2:
      kind: linux
      image: alpine

  links:
    - endpoints: ["r1:eth1", "r2:eth1"]

The ContainerLab extension allows topology deployment directly from the editor.

Right-click the topology file and select:

Deploy

To close your laboratory select the topology file again and select:

Destroy

Another way of using this, is by going directly to the ContainerLab tab in VSCode, choosing the undeployed lab, and deploying it from there.

To configure a router directly through its CLI, you can access it through the extension, selecting the SSH option.

To capture packets in your lab, choose the port where the capture will occur and select the Capture option.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Use Git for topology versioning
  • Keep configs in separate folders
  • Use consistent interface naming
  • Capture traffic frequently to troubleshoot your labs
  • Validate Linux bridges carefully
  • Document addressing schemes

docs.title: DTLS
docs.text: DTLS (Datagram Transport Layer Security) extends TLS to UDP-based applications while maintaining encryption and integrity protection.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• UDP support
  • TLS-based security
  • Packet loss tolerance
  • Replay protection
  • Low-latency encryption

docs.title: Common Use Cases
docs.text:
VoIPWebRTCIoTVPNs

Secure SIP and RTP communications.

Browser real-time communications.

Lightweight secure UDP traffic.

DTLS-based VPN tunnels.

docs.title: DTLS Architecture
docs.text:
graph LR
    A[Client] --> B[UDP Network]
    B --> C[DTLS Server]

docs.title: Topics Covered
docs.text:
• OpenSSL DTLS
  • DTLS handshakes
  • UDP encryption
  • Replay protection
  • Packet loss handling
  • DTLS troubleshooting

docs.title: Example DTLS Server
docs.text: openssl s_server -dtls -accept 4444 -cert cert.pem -key key.pem

docs.title: Example DTLS Client
docs.text:
openssl s_client -dtls -connect 127.0.0.1:4444

Note

DTLS is specifically designed to handle unreliable UDP transport.

docs.title: GNS3

  • Real-world networking operating systems

  • QEMU virtualization

docs.title: IPsec
docs.text: IPsec (Internet Protocol Security) is a Layer 3 security framework providing encryption, integrity, and authentication for IP traffic.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Component Purpose AH Authentication ESP Encryption IKE Key exchange SA Security Association

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
Transport ModeTunnel Mode

Encrypts the payload only.

Encrypts the full IP packet.

docs.title: Common Use Cases
docs.text:
• Site-to-site VPNs
  • Enterprise WAN security
  • Secure datacenter interconnects
  • Remote-access VPNs

docs.title: IPsec Architecture
docs.text:
graph LR
    A[LAN A] --> B[IPsec Gateway]
    B --> C[Encrypted Tunnel]
    C --> D[IPsec Gateway]
    D --> E[LAN B]

docs.title: Topics Covered
docs.text:
• IKEv2
  • ESP and AH
  • Tunnel vs transport mode
  • strongSwan
  • Linux IPsec
  • Routing integration
  • Troubleshooting

docs.title: Example strongSwan Service
docs.text:
sudo systemctl restart strongswan
sudo ip xfrm state

Note

ESP is significantly more common than AH in modern deployments.

docs.title: MACsec
docs.text:
MACsec (Media Access Control Security) is a Layer 2 encryption protocol defined by IEEE 802.1AE. It provides confidentiality, integrity, replay protection, and secure Ethernet transport between directly connected devices.

MACsec is commonly used in:

  • Datacenter fabrics
  • Service provider transport networks
  • Enterprise switching
  • Secure Ethernet backbones
  • Encrypted VLAN transport

docs.title: MACsec Overview
docs.text:
MACsec operates directly on Ethernet frames and encrypts traffic between neighboring devices.

Unlike IPsec, which operates at Layer 3, MACsec protects Layer 2 traffic transparently.

docs.title: MACsec Features
docs.text: Feature Description Encryption AES-GCM frame encryption Integrity Prevents frame tampering Replay Protection Drops replayed packets Layer Layer 2 Transparency No IP changes required

docs.title: MACsec Architecture
docs.text:
graph LR
    A[Host A] --> B[MACsec Switch/Router]
    B --> C[Encrypted Ethernet Link]
    C --> D[MACsec Switch/Router]
    D --> E[Host B]

docs.title: MKA Overview
docs.text:
MACsec itself only encrypts traffic.

The MACsec Key Agreement protocol (MKA), defined in IEEE 802.1X, handles:

  • Peer discovery
  • Authentication
  • Key exchange
  • Secure Association management
  • Rekeying

MKA automatically distributes encryption keys between MACsec peers.

docs.title: MKA Components
docs.text: Component Purpose CAK Connectivity Association Key CKN Connectivity Association Key Name SCI Secure Channel Identifier SAK Secure Association Key

docs.title: MKA Operation
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant R1
    participant R2

    R1->>R2: MKA Discovery
    R2->>R1: MKA Discovery
    R1->>R2: CAK/CKN Validation
    R2->>R1: CAK/CKN Validation
    R1->>R2: Secure Association Keys
    R2->>R1: MACsec Encrypted Traffic

docs.title: MACsec Laboratory
docs.text:
This laboratory demonstrates:

  • MACsec Connectivity Associations
  • Multiple encrypted Ethernet segments
  • IS-IS routing across MACsec links
  • VLAN transport
  • Host-to-host encrypted communication
  • SR SIM MACsec deployment inside Containerlab

docs.title: Topology Overview
docs.text:
graph LR

    HOST1 --> R1
    R1 --> CA1
    R2 --> CA1
    R4 --> CA1

    R2 --> CA2
    R3 --> CA2
    R4 --> CA2

    R3 --> HOST2

    subgraph CA1
        B1[MACBridge1]
    end

    subgraph CA2
        B2[MACBridge2]
    end

docs.title: Laboratory Goals
docs.text:
The objective of this laboratory is to:

  • Build two MACsec Connectivity Associations
  • Configure encrypted Layer 2 transport
  • Run IS-IS across MACsec links
  • Validate encrypted VLAN forwarding
  • Verify secure host communication

docs.title: Containerlab Topology File
docs.text:
Create the following file:

macsec-main-lab.clab.yml

docs.title: Topology Definition
docs.text:
name: macsec-main-lab
prefix: "x"

mgmt:
  network: macsec-main
  ipv4-subnet: 172.10.10.0/24

topology:
  kinds:
    nokia_srsim:
      type: sr-1x-48d
      image: localhost/nokia/srsim:25.10.R3
      license: SR_SIM_license_IST.txt

    linux:
      image: ghcr.io/srl-labs/network-multitool

  nodes:
    r1_macsec:
      kind: nokia_srsim
      startup-config: configs/r1.partial.cfg
      components:
        - slot: A
        - slot: 1

    r2_macsec:
      kind: nokia_srsim
      startup-config: configs/r2.partial.cfg
      components:
        - slot: A
        - slot: 1

    r3_macsec:
      kind: nokia_srsim
      startup-config: configs/r3.partial.cfg
      components:
        - slot: A
        - slot: 1

    r4_macsec:
      kind: nokia_srsim
      startup-config: configs/r4.partial.cfg
      components:
        - slot: A
        - slot: 1

    MACBridge1:
      kind: bridge

    MACBridge2:
      kind: bridge

    host1:
      kind: linux
      mgmt-ipv4: 172.10.10.31

    host2:
      kind: linux
      mgmt-ipv4: 172.10.10.32

  links:
    - endpoints: ["r1_macsec:1/1/c2/1", "MACBridge1:eth1"]
    - endpoints: ["r2_macsec:1/1/c2/1", "MACBridge1:eth2"]
    - endpoints: ["r4_macsec:1/1/c2/1", "MACBridge1:eth3"]

    - endpoints: ["r2_macsec:1/1/c3/1", "MACBridge2:eth4"]
    - endpoints: ["r3_macsec:1/1/c2/1", "MACBridge2:eth5"]
    - endpoints: ["r4_macsec:1/1/c3/1", "MACBridge2:eth6"]

    - endpoints: ["host1:eth1", "r1_macsec:1/1/c1/1"]
    - endpoints: ["host2:eth1", "r3_macsec:1/1/c1/1"]

docs.title: Connectivity Association 1
docs.text:
CA1 interconnects:

  • R1
  • R2
  • R4

Through:

MACBridge1

docs.title: Connectivity Association 2
docs.text:
CA2 interconnects:

  • R2
  • R3
  • R4

Through:

MACBridge2

docs.title: Routing Design
docs.text:
IS-IS is configured on all routers.

The routing domain enables:

Host1 <-> Host2

communication through encrypted MACsec segments.

docs.title: Define CAK and CKN
docs.text:
/system security
    macsec
        connectivity-association CA1
            cak 00112233445566778899AABBCCDDEEFF
            ckn CA1_KEY

docs.title: Enable MACsec on Interface
docs.text:
set / interface ethernet-1/1 admin-state enable

set / interface ethernet-1/1 ethernet
    macsec
        admin-state enable
        connectivity-association CA1

docs.title: Example IS-IS Configuration
docs.text:
set / network-instance default protocols isis instance CORE admin-state enable

set / network-instance default interface ethernet-1/1.0

docs.title: Start the Lab
docs.text: sudo containerlab deploy -t macsec-main-lab.clab.yml

docs.title: Verify Nodes
docs.text: docker ps

docs.title: Inspect Topology
docs.text: sudo containerlab inspect -t macsec-main-lab.clab.yml

docs.title: Verify MACsec Sessions
docs.text: show system security macsec connectivity-association

docs.title: Verify MKA
docs.text: show system security macsec mka

docs.title: Verify IS-IS Adjacencies
docs.text: show network-instance default protocols isis adjacency

docs.title: Verify Routing
docs.text: ping 192.168.10.2

docs.title: Traffic Validation
docs.text: Use packet captures to validate encryption.

docs.title: Capture on Linux Bridge
docs.text:
sudo tcpdump -i MACBridge1 -e

Encrypted MACsec frames should appear as:

EtherType 0x88e5

docs.title: Expected Results
docs.text: Validation Expected Result MKA Sessions Established MACsec CA Active IS-IS Adjacencies Up Host Connectivity Successful Packet Capture Encrypted frames

docs.title: MACsec Session Down
docs.text:
Verify:

  • Matching CAK
  • Matching CKN
  • Interface admin-state
  • L2 connectivity

docs.title: IS-IS Adjacency Failure
docs.text:
Verify:

  • MACsec operational state
  • Interface MTU
  • Subinterface configuration

docs.title: Host Connectivity Failure
docs.text:
Verify:

  • VLAN configuration
  • Default gateways
  • IS-IS routes

docs.title: Packet Capture Shows Cleartext
docs.text:
Possible causes:

  • MACsec not operational
  • Incorrect CA association
  • Interface not encrypted

Warning

Linux bridges may filter MACsec EtherTypes unless multicast and forwarding behavior are adjusted appropriately.

Note

MACsec in WAN mode preserves VLAN headers in cleartext while encrypting Ethernet payloads.

docs.title: SSH
docs.text: SSH (Secure Shell) is a secure remote access and tunnelling protocol widely used for Linux administration, automation, and secure transport.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Encrypted remote access
  • Public key authentication
  • Secure file transfer
  • Port forwarding
  • Tunnelling support

docs.title: Common SSH Services
docs.text: Service Purpose SSH Remote shell SCP Secure copy SFTP Secure file transfer SSH Tunnel Encrypted forwarding

docs.title: SSH Architecture
docs.text:
graph LR
    A[SSH Client] --> B[Encrypted Session]
    B --> C[SSH Server]

docs.title: Topics Covered
docs.text:
• SSH key authentication
  • SSH hardening
  • SCP and SFTP
  • Port forwarding
  • SSH tunnelling
  • Linux administration
  • Troubleshooting

docs.title: Generate SSH Keys
docs.text: ssh-keygen -t ed25519

docs.title: Connect to a Server
docs.text: ssh user@192.168.1.10

docs.title: Example SSH Tunnel
docs.text:
ssh -L 8080:localhost:80 user@server

Warning

Password authentication should be disabled in production environments whenever possible.

docs.title: TLS
docs.text: TLS (Transport Layer Security) secures application traffic over TCP networks and is the foundation of HTTPS and many secure application protocols.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Encryption
  • Authentication
  • Integrity validation
  • Certificate-based trust
  • Perfect Forward Secrecy

docs.title: Common Protocols Using TLS
docs.text: Protocol Usage HTTPS Secure web SMTPS Secure email FTPS Secure file transfer MQTT TLS IoT security

docs.title: TLS Handshake
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Server

    Client->>Server: ClientHello
    Server->>Client: ServerHello + Certificate
    Client->>Server: Key Exchange
    Server->>Client: Secure Session Established

docs.title: Topics Covered
docs.text:
• OpenSSL
  • TLS certificates
  • Certificate Authorities
  • CSR generation
  • Cipher suites
  • TLS debugging
  • HTTPS testing

docs.title: Example OpenSSL Test
docs.text:
openssl s_client -connect google.com:443

Warning

Self-signed certificates are suitable for labs but not production environments.

docs.title: WireGuard
docs.text: WireGuard is a modern Layer 3 VPN protocol focused on simplicity, performance, and cryptographic security.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Minimal configuration
  • High performance
  • Modern cryptography
  • UDP-based transport
  • Simple key management
  • Cross-platform support

docs.title: Cryptography
docs.text: Component Algorithm Key Exchange Curve25519 Encryption ChaCha20 Authentication Poly1305 Hashing BLAKE2s

docs.title: Typical Use Cases
docs.text:
Site-to-Site VPNRemote AccessLab TopologiesContainer Networking

Connect remote networks securely.

Secure remote user connectivity.

Encrypted routing experiments.

Secure inter-container communication.

docs.title: Example Topology
docs.text:
graph LR
    A[WG Node 1] --- B[Internet]
    B --- C[WG Node 2]

docs.title: Topics Covered
docs.text:
• Linux WireGuard setup
  • Peer configuration
  • OSPF over WireGuard
  • Routing integration
  • MTU tuning
  • Containerlab deployment
  • Troubleshooting

docs.title: Example Configuration
docs.text:
[Interface]
Address = 10.10.10.1/24
PrivateKey = <private-key>
ListenPort = 51820

[Peer]
PublicKey = <peer-public-key>
AllowedIPs = 10.10.10.2/32
Endpoint = 192.168.1.10:51820

Warning

Incorrect MTU values commonly cause fragmentation and tunnel instability.
